summary: Curry County ground lookout on Bosley Butte, registered as built around 1940; burned in 2012 and replaced by a detection camera. No current access described.

facts.design: Ground-level cab on the summit; the register lists L-4 cabs (1940, 1954) and an Amort cab (1984), while other sources date a new cab to 1987
facts.status_note: The cab burned down in 2012. The Coos Forest Protective Association did not plan to replace it and had a detection camera on the summit.
facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry (register); Coos Forest Protective Association ran the later camera

events.note: Camp on the site (a rag camp, per the register)
Register's year for the first L-4 ground cabin; a June 1941 newspaper describes the station being built that year
Fire warden supervised building the new lookout station atop Bosley Butte (Port Orford Post, June 27, 1941)
L-4 cab replaced by another L-4 (register); a 14 x 14 ground house is listed in the 1954 district report
Register gives an Amort cab in 1984
Other sources date a new cab to 1987 (ODF cab; State-designed house on a short leveling tower)
Lightning strike destroyed the communications antenna; fuses worked and the damage was limited to the antenna
Coos FPA installed a smoke detecting camera system on the lookout
The 1987 ODF cab was being staffed every summer and was still there in 2010
Fire destroyed the lookout structure in spring 2012; cause under investigation, vandalism suspected

corrections.why: The June 11, 1941 item calls the station 'planned this year' and the June 27, 1941 item describes its building, so no source read confirms a 1940 build. The register's 1940 is kept in the story as a disagreement; a human should decide.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1940 for the first L-4 cab; a June 1941 newspaper item describes the new station being built that year. Both are stated in the story and the record's 1940 is flagged.
The register gives an Amort cab in 1984; the Forest Lookouts page and firelookout.com date a new cab to 1987. Both are stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: Status 'gone' stands: the lookout burned in 2012. The record's '2012 removed' is really a fire loss, so the event is recorded as burned. The build year (1940 in the register, 1941 in a newspaper) and the later cab dates (1984 vs 1987) disagree; the proposed build-year correction needs a human decision. No source read after 2012 describes the summit, so current condition and public access are unknown; access is left out of facts. Coos Forest Protective Association runs the camera and is not the record's agency. Used 0 WebSearch calls and about 5 page reads.
